security_audit.summary: Most presented alerts are benign Playwright examples; no evidence found of keylogging, prompt injection, or malicious exfiltration in reviewed context. Confirmed risks involve unguarded database operations, predictable temporary files, and indiscriminate process termination; HAR commit guidance adds a data-disclosure concern. All 400 presented findings were adjudicated; 888 omitted matches still require manual review before automatic publication. Static review was capped at 400/1288 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 888 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Database teardown and snapshot restoration lack explicit test-database target validation.
remediation.suggestion: Reject non-test database targets and require explicit destructive-operation approval. Prefer disposable databases and argument-array execution over shell-based restore commands.

remediation.issue: The temporary fixture uses a predictable shared /tmp filename without exclusive creation.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary directory with mkdtemp and restrictive permissions. Use exclusive file creation and remove the directory during teardown.

remediation.issue: The CI cleanup command force-kills all processes associated with port 3000.
remediation.suggestion: Track the test server PID and verify process ownership before termination. Prefer graceful shutdown or Playwright-managed server lifecycle.

remediation.issue: The HAR maintenance guide recommends commits without a redaction requirement.
remediation.suggestion: Use synthetic accounts and sanitize HAR headers, cookies, query parameters, and bodies before committing. Add secret checks for recorded fixtures.

remediation.issue: The static review catalog excludes 888 additional matches.
remediation.suggestion: Complete manual adjudication of the omitted matches before automatic publication. Do not treat this capped review as clearance of the entire scan.

semantic_findings.description: The guide says 'Commit `.har` files to version control' after recording staging admin API traffic. Without redaction, recordings can disclose authorization headers, cookies, or sensitive response bodies through repository history.

content.value_statement: Fragile tests and inconsistent setup make browser testing difficult to maintain. This skill provides practical Playwright patterns for test design, debugging, and CI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guide locator selection and auto-waiting assertions for resilient end-to-end tests.
Design reusable fixtures, page objects, authentication setup, and isolated test data.
Explain API interception, third-party mocking, OAuth flows, and multi-user scenarios.
Provide examples for accessibility, visual regression, browser APIs, Electron, and extension testing.
Diagnose flaky tests with traces, request monitoring, and repeated runs.
Outline CI pipelines, Docker execution, sharding, coverage collection, and performance budgets.
limitations: Provides reference guidance, not a bundled browser runner or managed testing service.
Requires a configured project, Playwright dependencies, browsers, and access to the application under test.
Examples require adaptation to application routes, selectors, credentials, framework versions, and CI infrastructure.
Does not guarantee test stability, complete accessibility coverage, or safe execution of database cleanup examples.

use_cases.title: Add Maintainable Browser Tests
use_cases.description: Create application tests with accessible locators, reusable setup, and assertions tied to visible behavior.

use_cases.title: Investigate Intermittent Failures
use_cases.description: Review flaky tests for timing errors, shared state, unstable selectors, and missing network synchronization.

use_cases.title: Improve CI Test Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan browser installation, caching, sharding, reports, and controlled environment setup for automated test runs.

prompt_templates.title: Write a First Browser Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Playwright test for the login flow in this project. Use accessible locators and auto-waiting assertions. Identify missing application details before assuming selectors.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: adding a first end-to-end test

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Flaky Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this failing Playwright test and its error output. Identify timing, locator, and isolation problems. Propose focused fixes and repeated-run verification without hiding failures.

prompt_templates.title: Design Authentication Fixtures
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Playwright fixtures for admin and member workflows in this project. Isolate worker data and protect saved authentication state. Explain which external services need mocks.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Sharded CI Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Playwright CI configuration for sharding, caching, reports, and database lifecycle. Restrict destructive operations to disposable test resources. Require approval before destructive changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: reviewing CI reliability and safety

output_examples.input: A checkout test sometimes fails after clicking Submit.
output: Diagnosis: the assertion runs before the checkout response updates the page.
Recommended change: register the response wait before clicking, then assert the confirmation heading.
Verification: repeat the test and inspect traces for any remaining ordering failures.

output_examples.input: Plan a faster Playwright workflow for our CI pipeline.
output: Execution plan: divide tests across shards and isolate data by worker.
Dependency plan: align browser binaries with the installed Playwright version and cache them using the dependency lockfile.
Reporting plan: retain failure traces and merge shard reports into one result.
Safety check: verify disposable database targets before reset or restore operations.

best_practices: Use accessible locators and auto-waiting assertions that describe observable application behavior.
Isolate test data and authentication state; keep credentials and sanitized recordings out of unintended publication paths.
Review destructive setup commands before execution and verify changes with targeted, repeated test runs.
anti_patterns: Replacing reliable synchronization with fixed sleeps or excessive retries.
Sharing mutable users, sessions, or database state across parallel workers without isolation.
Running database resets against unverified targets or committing recordings without secret redaction.

faq.question: Does this skill install Playwright or run browsers automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Browser execution requires an available tool environment, installed dependencies, and project configuration.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for all three tools. Available file access and command execution depend on your configured environment.

faq.question: Which test types does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers end-to-end, API, component, visual, accessibility, security, and performance testing, with additional Electron and browser extension examples.

faq.question: Can it help with flaky tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents trace analysis, locator improvements, synchronization, test isolation, and repeated runs. Application-specific evidence is still required.

faq.question: Should every service be mocked?
faq.answer: No. The guidance favors real application integrations and controlled mocks for external services. Select boundaries according to the behavior under test.

faq.question: Are database cleanup examples safe to copy unchanged?
faq.answer: No. Validate disposable test targets and require approval for destructive operations. Protect credentials, saved sessions, and recorded traffic before sharing artifacts.
